name: CRUCIBLE Auric Sovereign Bespoke Arm
description:
The Crucible Auric Sovereign is a fully hand-built luxury cyberlimb, each unit commissioned individually and constructed over 8-12 weeks by Crucible's master artisans from the client's exact anatomical and aesthetic specifications. The structural chassis is 18-karat gold-infused palladium alloy — structurally superior to steel while carrying a warmth and luster that reads unmistakably as precious metal — overlaid with hand-engraved motifs negotiated with the client and set with genuine gemstone inlays at the knuckle joints. A synthetic dermis option is available in any skin tone or pattern, but most clients at this price point choose to leave the metalwork exposed as the statement it is.

The Auric Sovereign is purchased exclusively by tier 5 Spire elite — executives, heirs, celebrity artists, and political figures for whom the arm is as much a declaration of status as any piece of jewelry. Crucible maintains a waitlist measured in years and does not accept unsolicited orders. The functional specifications are excellent but unremarkable; the point is not performance, it is provenance. A Crucible serial number is verifiable, and forgeries exist — poorly.
installation_requirements: Full shoulder disarticulation, Crucible-approved surgical partner clinic, dedicated pre-op anatomical scan session at Crucible atelier
rejection_risk: Minimal — palladium-alloy chassis has exceptional biocompatibility; Crucible includes a Lazarus Pharmaceuticals rejection-suppression protocol in the base commission price
maintenance: Annual atelier service visit required; includes gemstone inspection, engraving touch-up, firmware update, and neural calibration; Crucible covers first 5 years under commission warranty
specifications: {"arm_weight": "3.1 kg", "chassis_material": "18-karat gold-infused palladium alloy", "surface_finish": "hand-engraved, client-specified motifs", "gemstone_inlays": "genuine, client-selected, at knuckle and wrist joints", "grip_strength": "720 N sustained", "neural_latency": "7 ms", "dermis_option": "synthetic, any tone or pattern", "commission_lead_time": "8-12 weeks", "units_produced_annually": "<40 worldwide"}
side_effects: Palladium alloy conducts electrical charge slightly more readily than standard chassis materials — static discharge events are more frequent and occasionally startling
Gemstone inlays at knuckle joints create minor pressure points during sustained gripping tasks
The arm's recognizability makes the wearer an immediate target for kidnapping, robbery, or political statement violence
Neural calibration drift is more pronounced if the owner travels frequently between climate zones due to alloy thermal sensitivity
cultural_context: In Meridian's Spire tier, a Crucible arm on someone's shoulder ends conversations and starts them simultaneously — it signals wealth beyond what most people will earn in a lifetime. The Auric Sovereign specifically is whispered about in tier 3-4 aspirational circles the way old-world luxury cars once were: an object of desire that marks an almost incomprehensible distance.
known_users: Tier 5 corporate executives and board members
Spire-tier celebrity performers and media figures
Political figures and hereditary wealth families
Collectors who commission units as wearable art without functional need
story_hooks: A Crucible Auric Sovereign arm is recovered from a crime scene with the owner nowhere to be found — the serial number traces to someone officially listed as dead for three years
A flawless forgery of a Crucible arm appears in the tier 3 markets, impossibly accurate — either Crucible has a leak or someone reverse-engineered the process entirely
A Spire executive's Auric Sovereign is publicly damaged in an assassination attempt; the political fallout over who targeted them pulls the party into Spire-level intrigue
